questions.stemEn: A child has recurrent periumbilical pain that is sometimes sharp and sometimes dull. It occurs mainly during play and improves with rest and lying down. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Functional abdominal pain. يصف هذا النوع بأنه غالبًا periumbilical أو poorly localized، يأتي على نوبات قصيرة، ويكون الطفل طبيعيًا بين النوبات مع غياب alarm features.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Pancreatitis لا يتماشى مع طفل طبيعي بين النوبات ولا توجد في الـstem قرائن عضوية أو مخبرية تدعمه.
questions.clinicalPearl: Recurrent periumbilical pain without alarm features commonly represents a functional abdominal pain disorder.

tts.text: A child has recurrent periumbilical pain that is sometimes sharp and sometimes dull. It occurs mainly during play and improves with rest and lying down. What is the most likely cause? Option A. Functional abdominal pain. Option B. Pancreatitis.

questions.stemEn: A child has recurrent periumbilical pain for nine months. He is otherwise completely well, has no alarm signs, and is normal between episodes. What is the next step?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Reassurance عندما يكون الألم المزمن متكررًا بلا alarm symptoms ولا توجد دلائل على مرض عضوي. لا يوصي المصدر بإجراء تصوير روتيني في هذا السياق.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Upper GI study وCT لا يوصي بهما المصدر في غياب red flags أو دلائل مرض عضوي.
questions.clinicalPearl: Absence of alarm symptoms usually argues against routine imaging in functional abdominal pain.

questions.subtopic: Functional abdominal pain disorder / abdominal migraine
questions.stemEn: A 13-year-old girl has frequent vomiting and periumbilical abdominal pain and has missed 60 days of school. Prior gastroenterology investigations were unrevealing, and her current symptoms improve with antiemetics and hydration. What should be included in the discharge plan?

options.text: Exercise and close follow-up with psychology

questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار referral for cognitive behavioral therapy، ويربط السيناريو بـfunctional abdominal pain disorders/abdominal migraine بعد استبعاد سبب عضوي مهم. يذكر أن CBT قد تساعد الطفل على التعامل ذاتيًا مع الألم المتكرر.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: إعادة الإحالة وحدها إلى gastroenterology لا تضيف كثيرًا بعد workup سلبي بحسب المصدر، وantiemetics وحدها لا تعالج الجانب الوظيفي المتكرر.
questions.clinicalPearl: CBT is a source-supported option for recurrent functional abdominal pain disorders.

tts.text: A 13-year-old girl has frequent vomiting and periumbilical abdominal pain and has missed 60 days of school. Prior gastroenterology investigations were unrevealing, and her current symptoms improve with antiemetics and hydration. What should be included in the discharge plan? Option A. Antiemetics for future episodes. Option B. Exercise and close follow-up with psychology. Option C. Referral for cognitive behavioral therapy. Option D. Referral to gastroenterology clinic.
